target_customer: Urban Indonesian households buying groceries and traditional wet market merchants who sell through the app
problem: Shoppers cannot easily buy from many merchants in a traditional market in one order, and merchants, often older sellers, lack digital storefronts.
business_model: Hyperlocal marketplace with personal shoppers, take rate and delivery fees, plus B2B2C partnerships with market operators

founders.name: Henri Suhardja
previous_startups: Describes himself as a second time entrepreneur (earlier company not named)
founders.background_notes: Angel investor in food MSMEs per YC page.

founders.name: Ong Tek Tjan
founders.background_notes: YC page states he was born in 1969; age is that year subtracted from the 2017 founding year. Over 26 years in SME and commercial banking.

competitors.name: Segari
competitors.what: E-grocery startup delivering groceries in Indonesia
competitors.funding_then: $16M Series A in 2021 backed by Go-Ventures and Alfamart

competitors.name: Sayurbox
competitors.what: Online grocery sourcing produce directly from farmers

competitors.name: HappyFresh
competitors.what: Online grocery delivery using personal shoppers from supermarkets

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace and shopper apps with merchant onboarding; the difficulty is operations and merchant digitization rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Relationships with market operators and merchant onboarding by field helpers called Explorers are hard to replicate quickly, though the app itself is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Titipku remained independent and partnered with market operators and local government into 2026.

market_need_then: Indonesia has about 16,000 local markets with 8 million merchants per the company, and a June 2020 Nielsen survey reported in press found 58 percent of people preferred traditional markets even during the pandemic.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as Instacart for local markets (Product Hunt tagline, August 2021)

branding.brand_signature: Explorers, the people who onboard older merchants onto the app
branding.community_and_virality: Local press coverage of market digitization partnerships; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Local Indonesian name with steady regional press but no evidence of wide consumer awareness.

outcome_analysis: Titipku digitized over 150 traditional markets and 10,000 traders in Greater Jakarta by 2025 per press, working through market operators and officials. No disclosed funding beyond the YC deal and no exit were found, so it appears to be a slow, capital light operator rather than a venture scaled marketplace.
notes: The only funding found is the standard YC deal of about $125K for 7 percent (September 2021, listed by Seedtable as a seed round); aggregators disagree on dates and number of rounds (Persana says 3 rounds, Briter dates the YC deal January 2021), all unverified. The standard deal is not recorded as a round. DailySocial article on traction returned 503. Competitor funding figures come from the Jakarta Post piece dated September 2021, two months after the batch. Name origin not sourced.
